name: Numerical calibrations definition
purpose: cap holds the points of the numerical calibration curves declared in caf: one record per raw/engineering value pair. SCOS-2000 calibrates a raw value by locating it between two consecutive points of the curve and interpolating linearly between them (as the CAF_INTER description of ICD 6.7/6.9 explains). Outside the range covered by the points it either extrapolates from the first or last two points or returns an invalid value, depending on the curve's CAF_INTER flag. Raw values are written in the format declared by CAF_RAWFMT and, for unsigned integers, in the radix given by CAF_RADIX. Engineering values follow CAF_ENGFMT and are always decimal, even when they are unsigned integers. Because the key is the pair (CAP_NUMBR, CAP_XVALS), a curve cannot contain two points with the same raw value. The number of records per curve should agree with CAF_NCURVE.

fields.name: CAP_NUMBR
fields.description: Identifier of the calibration curve this point belongs to; must match CAF_NUMBR of an existing caf record.

fields.name: CAP_XVALS
fields.description: Raw value of the calibration point, written in a format compatible with CAF_RAWFMT. Unsigned integer raw values (CAF_RAWFMT = 'U') must be written in the radix of the curve (CAF_RADIX).

fields.name: CAP_YVALS
fields.description: Engineering value of the calibration point, written in a format compatible with CAF_ENGFMT. All engineering values, including unsigned integers, are written in decimal whatever the curve's CAF_RADIX.

history: ICD 5.1 ('Numerical calibration curves definition: cap', p. 33) has the same three fields but CAP_NUMBR is Number(4). The identifier became Char(10) in ICD 6.0 (ICD 7.0 Annex 1, p. 247; field-type change also listed for 6.2/6.3, p. 253). The definition is unchanged in ICD 6.7 Draft A (p. 63-64), 6.9 (p. 66-67) and 7.0 (p. 68). pyscos2000 (ICD 7.2) matches: three mandatory fields, key CAP_NUMBR + CAP_XVALS.
notes: No discrepancy between ICD 7.0 and pyscos2000. Solar Orbiter 2025-09-16: 7,830 points for 679 curves (every CAP_NUMBR exists in caf and every curve has at least 2 points; the largest has 1,024). Raw values reach the full 14-character field width, as do engineering values. Example (real data): curve CAHP0000TM maps raw -2048 to -180 and raw 2047 to 179.91211, a two-point linear calibration.
